einstellungen.text: An old man believes nobody is waiting for him. And he couldn't be more wrong.
You sit down next to your grandpa on the hospital bed.
“We are, Grandpa. We're waiting. Every Sunday from now on.”
Grandpa looks at you for a long time. “Every Sunday? You've all got so much going on.”
Lina crosses her arms. “You have no idea how boring the internet is.”
Grandpa laughs so loud the nurse sticks her head in the door.
Forty afternoons, you thought. If you come every Sunday, that turns into hundreds.
The first Sunday. Mom bakes. Dad burns the potatoes. Grandpa eats three plates anyway.
The phones stay in the fruit bowl. Nobody misses them.
The second Sunday, Ben brings his mom. And the old radio man comes too.
He says his Sunday hasn't been this full in twenty years.
Grandpa and him start arguing about soccer right away. Like two old friends.
In the summer, you all go to the lake together. Grandpa tells stories you've never heard before.
And you realize: you almost missed every single one of them.
Not because of a storm. Because of one single word. Later.
The network has been back for a long time now. But Sunday stays.
For three days, the whole world went quiet.
And that's exactly when you started talking to each other again.
